# Variant C — "Living constellation"

*Mockup:* `index.html` (self-contained; generated by `build.py`)
*Renders:* `dark.png`, `light.png` — 1440 px wide, full page, both themes.

---

## 1. Concept

A constellation drawn as a printed circuit, where **the junctions are stars**. Variant C takes the
four-point sparkle out of the ART logo and makes it the atom of the whole system: every place a trace
begins, bends meaningfully, or ends is a sparkle. The hero is one continuous sentence read left to
right — *a star field and an eight-node asterism → four of its nodes routed on copper into a chip
labelled MODEL (which holds a small constellation of its own) → a posterior blooming out the far
side*. That is literally Josh's job description drawn once, at large size, on the front page.

Everywhere else the same three primitives (trace, pad/via, star) drop to gridline weight: a card's
accent stripe becomes a hairline rail broken by one star; a section divider becomes a trace that ends
in a drilled via instead of stopping dead; the biography rail forks and rejoins where two roles
overlap. **The motif is loud exactly once and structural everywhere else.**

---

## 2. Tokens

### Added (7)

| Token | Dark | Light | Meaning — never reassigned |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--trace` | `#414d80` | `#aeb2c8` | **Front copper.** Structural routing: card rails, timeline, dividers, chip outline, chart leader lines. |
| `--trace-2` | `#212a4c` | `#cfd1dc` | **Back layer / silkscreen.** Sky links between stars, chart gridlines, board-edge pads, inner die outlines. |
| `--trace-lit` | `#6f7fd8` | `#8d84cf` | A routed signal that is *live but not pulsing*: brand mark strokes, kicker numerals, nav underline. |
| `--star-dim` | `#8e9ad0` | `#8b90a8` | An unlit node — star field, chart markers, past timeline events. |
| `--star-lit` | `#e9edff` | `#3a2f8f` | A lit node — the current role, the mode of the posterior, the endpoint of a series. |
| `--glow` | `rgba(139,123,255,.55)` | `transparent` | Dark-only bloom, applied as `drop-shadow` on `.st-lit`. |
| `--halo` | `transparent` | `rgba(91,67,214,.26)` | Light-only 1 px ring around a lit node. |
| `--pad` | `rgba(255,255,255,.05)` | `#f1f0ea` | Fill for chips, the chip body, and icon wells. |

`--glow` / `--halo` are a deliberate pair: **one CSS rule, two designed answers.** Dark says "lit" with
a bloom; light says "lit" with a ring. Neither theme is the other inverted, and neither uses hue alone
— size and a second channel always carry the same information (greyscale proof is in Panel 01).

### Unchanged

Every existing token in `tokens.json` survives, including all four category hues
(`--cat-sla` / `--cat-ii` / `--cat-ic` / `--cat-du`) and `--cat-sec`. The new copper tokens are
deliberately *cool* (indigo-slate, not amber-copper) so they cannot be confused with the
Discovery & Understanding amber.

---

## 3. Motif rules

**Stroke weights** — four, and only four:

| Weight | Name | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 px | hairline | sky links, silkscreen grids, chart gridlines, inner die outlines |
| 1.5 px | front copper | everything structural: rails, dividers, timeline, chip body, icons at 24–40 px |
| 1.75 px | signal | routed feeds in the hero (`--trace-lit`) |
| 2 px | series / pulse | the chart line and the travelling pulses — the only 2 px in the system |

**Corner radius** on a routed trace = `2 × stroke width`, rounded to the grid:
hero routes `r = 8–12`, timeline branch `r = 11`, dividers `r = 6`, small UI `r = 4–5`, icons
`r = 1.6–2.2` (24 u grid), brand mark `r = 2.5` (32 u grid). Bends are **45° or 90° only** — no free
angles anywhere in the system.

**Stars (`#star`)** — one path, one concavity constant (`k = 0.17 R`). Size is the hierarchy:

| Size | Role |
|---|---|
| 5–7 px | quiet punctuation: chip dots, kicker star, chart markers, card rail |
| 9–11 px | a node that names something: divider junction, timeline event, card category |
| 13–17 px | a lit node: current role, hero hub, chart endpoint |
| 20–22 px | the mode of the posterior — the single largest star on the site |

**Vias (`#via`)** — a real drilled annulus (outer 3.4 u, hole 1.5 u, `fill-rule: evenodd`), rendered at
6–9 px. **One token, one meaning:** a *star* is a node that carries meaning (a paper, an event, a
signal); a *via* is a pass-through — the end of a rule, a fork in the timeline, where a trace changes
layer. They are never interchangeable.

**Spacing** stays on the existing 4 px scale (`--space-1..9`). New rhythms: card rail inset 14 px;
timeline branch offset 22 px; timeline event pitch 132 px; board-edge pad 34 × 7 px at a 62 px pitch.

**Motion** — two loops only. Pulses (`26 900` dash, 7 s linear, staggered 1.35 s) travel the four hero
feeds; lit stars breathe (opacity .68 → 1, 9 s ease-in-out alternate). Both are cancelled by
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and the static frame *is* the frame in `dark.png` — nothing depends
on being seen in motion. Nothing outside the hero animates.

---

## 4. What to retire

1. **The 3 px coloured card stripe.** Replaced by a neutral 1.5 px rail whose single star carries the
   hue. The current stripe spends the loudest element on the least specific information.
2. **The pill chip with a coloured dot.** Chips become square-ish pads (5 px radius) with a 9 px star.
   Only *states* (student-led, NOW) get a filled background; *categories* never do.
3. **The pseudo-log citations axis** (100 / 500 / 1,000 / 2,000 / 3,000). It flattens a decade of
   growth and misreports the shape. Linear axis, direct label on the endpoint, legend deleted.
4. **Legend-only labelling** in the publication figures generally — every series that can be labelled
   in place should be.
5. **Plain 1 px `border-top` dividers.** Replaced by a trace that terminates in a via.
6. **The generic `✦` glyph in the nav lockup.** Replaced by the reduced triad mark.
7. **The decorative hero line-web.** It reads as "generic tech background"; the new hero reads as a
   diagram of the research.

---

## 5. Implementation notes

- **Paint contract for `<symbol>`/`<use>`.** Document CSS selectors do **not** reach into a `<use>`
  shadow tree, so every symbol paints itself using the two *inherited* paint properties only —
  `stroke` for routing, `fill` for stars and vias. Callers set both on the `<use>` element
  (`class="ico i-sla"` → `stroke: var(--trace-lit); fill: var(--cat-sla)`). One symbol therefore
  serves both colours, both themes, and every size. No `context-fill`, no duplicated symbols, no
  custom-property tricks that vary by engine.
- **Optical stroke scaling.** Symbol paths carry `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"`; `stroke-width`
  is inherited from the `<use>` in CSS pixels. Icons: 1.5 px @ 24–40, 2 px @ 48–72, 2.5 px @ 96. The
  brand mark is the one element whose weight tracks size (3 / 2 / 1.6 px at 96 / 44 / 32).
- **Brand mark.** Six stars on a 32 u grid, one continuous route: `N3→N4→N5` draws a **J** (stem +
  hook), `N1→N2→N3→N6` lays a shallow **S** across the top. At **24 px and below** it reduces to the
  core triad (shoulder, hub, tail) — that is the favicon-16, the nav lockup and the footer mark.
  Both live as `#mark` / `#mark-min` in a single sprite.
- **Geometry is generated, not hand-drawn.** `build.py` holds a `route(points, r)` filleting helper
  (quadratic corners), `star_path(R, k)`, the posterior contour function and the deterministic star
  field (LCG, fixed seed → byte-identical builds). Porting to the site means moving ~90 lines into
  `build_html.py` next to `_citations_svg`.
- **Charts.** The whole chart stays inline SVG built in Python, as today — `pubchart.js` still only
  adds tooltips. The star marker is a `<use href="#star">`, so tooltip hit targets can simply be
  larger transparent circles on top.
- **Hero cost.** One inline SVG, ~600 nodes, no canvas, no library, no runtime fetch — it is part of
  the pre-rendered SEO layer. The current `<canvas>` hero script can be deleted.
- **Accessibility.** All body/label text is unchanged token pairs (AA in both themes). The hero SVG is
  `aria-hidden`; the composition's meaning is carried by the silkscreen labels DATA / MODEL /
  POSTERIOR and by the H1 copy. Category information is never hue-only: chips carry the full name,
  timeline states carry the "NOW" pad, the chart endpoint carries its number.

---

## 6. Risks

- **The die-inside-the-chip detail** (a five-star asterism inside the MODEL block) is charming at
  1440 px and turns to mush below ~900 px. The mobile hero must drop the die and probably the outer
  two posterior contours; plan a `viewBox` crop (sky + chip only) rather than a uniform scale.
- **`--star-lit` in light is a deep violet**, which is close in feel to `--cat-sla`. It never appears
  next to an SLA chip in these panels, but a page that puts a lit star beside a violet category badge
  will read ambiguously. Rule: lit stars and category stars never occupy the same 24 px.
- **Two layers can become three.** The moment someone adds a "medium" trace weight the drawing stops
  reading as a board. Keep the four stroke weights above as a hard list in the stylesheet comment.
- **Pulse fatigue.** Four pulses on a 7 s loop is calm; the same device on cards or nav would be
  intolerable. Motion is hero-only, by rule.
- **The 68 % leader line** crosses two outer contours. Acceptable as an annotated contour plot, but if
  the contour count ever grows, move both labels into a legend row beside POSTERIOR.
- **Favicon legibility at 16 px** depends on the reduced triad; if the tail star is ever dropped the
  mark stops reading as a hook and becomes a generic sparkle pair. Ship the triad as its own asset,
  do not let a build step downscale the six-star mark.
